name_en: Chicken 65 (Sri Lankan Style Spicy Fried Chicken)
regional_origin: Colombo (South Indian origin, adopted into Sri Lankan restaurant and home cooking)

ingredients.name: Boneless chicken thighs
ingredients.notes: cut into 3cm cubes; thighs stay juicier than breast during deep frying

ingredients.name: Plain yogurt (curd)
ingredients.notes: 3-4 tablespoons; acts as a tenderiser and helps the marinade cling to the chicken

ingredients.name: Kashmiri red chilli powder
ingredients.notes: use Kashmiri for deep colour with moderate heat; regular chilli powder gives more heat but less colour

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: made into a paste with the ginger

ingredients.name: Ginger
ingredients.notes: made into a paste with the garlic

ingredients.name: Rice flour
ingredients.notes: for coating before frying; rice flour gives a crispier exterior than wheat flour

ingredients.name: Cornflour (cornstarch)
ingredients.notes: combined with rice flour for the crispiest coating

ingredients.name: Curry leaves
ingredients.notes: 2 sprigs; for the final temper -- curry leaves are considered essential to the dish's character

steps.instruction: In a bowl, combine the yogurt, Kashmiri chilli powder, garam masala, cumin powder, turmeric, garlic-ginger paste, lime juice, and salt. Mix well into a smooth marinade.
Add the chicken cubes to the marinade and toss to coat thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight. Bring to room temperature 20-30 minutes before frying.
Just before frying, add the rice flour and cornflour to the marinated chicken. Toss well so every piece is coated in a thin, even layer. The coating should be light -- tap off any excess.
Heat the oil to 160-170C (320-340F). Fry the chicken in small batches for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through and golden. Do not overcrowd the pan. Drain on paper towels.

For the final temper: heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a separate small pan. Add the curry leaves (they will crackle loudly) and the slit green chillies. Fry for 30-60 seconds until the curry leaves are crispy.
Pour the tempered curry leaves and chillies over the fried chicken pieces. Toss briefly to combine. Serve immediately, garnished with lime wedges and sliced raw onions.

source_site: islandsmile.org, cross-checked against myfoodstory.com, swasthi's recipes, yummytummyaarthi.com, marionskitchen.com, sinfullyspicy.com, teaforturmeric.com, and shanas.kitchen
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 8+ independent sources from both Sri Lankan and South Indian food blogs; strong agreement on yogurt marinade, rice+cornflour coating, and the essential curry leaf temper at the end
notes: Chicken 65 originated in Chennai (Tamil Nadu, India) and has been enthusiastically adopted into Sri Lankan restaurant and home cooking, particularly popular with the Tamil community and increasingly island-wide. The name's origin is debated -- popular theories include 65 spices, 65-day-old chickens, or a hotel menu item number from 1965. Like thosai (sl_074), this is a South Indian dish deeply embedded in Sri Lankan Tamil food culture. The combination of rice flour AND cornflour for the coating is the most consistently recommended technique across sources -- rice flour alone gives crispiness, cornflour gives the light, airy texture; using wheat flour alone produces a heavier crust. The curry leaf temper at the end is considered non-negotiable by almost every source and is what gives chicken 65 its signature fragrance distinguishing it from other fried chicken.
